Definition: of Latin origin; a denarius (or ten asses):--pence, penny(-worth).
BiblicalUsage: The denarius was a day's wage for a labourer, the coin ordinary people handled every day. It is the wage promised in the vineyard parable, the coin handed to Jesus when they ask about taxes, the two coins the good Samaritan leaves for the wounded man, and the three hundred pence Judas thought the ointment was worth.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the denarius shows how plainly Jesus talked about money. He used the coin in every man's pocket to teach about fairness, about what belongs to Caesar and what belongs to God, and about the worth of a life poured out in love.
